candidates.name: improve-codebase-architecture
candidates.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

candidates.name: pr
candidates.description: Use when writing a PR body.

candidates.name: prototype
candidates.description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

candidates.name: research
candidates.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.

candidates.name: retro
candidates.description: Conduct a retrospective on a coding session.

candidates.name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
candidates.description: Configure this repo for the engineering skills: set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.

candidates.name: tdd
candidates.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

candidates.name: to-spec
candidates.description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.

candidates.name: to-tickets
candidates.description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker (edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker).

candidates.name: triage
candidates.description: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles, categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

candidates.name: wayfinder
candidates.description: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

candidates.name: wizard
candidates.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.

candidates.name: chief-of-staff
candidates.description: Pursue a long-running goal in a single session by co-ordinating subagents.

candidates.name: claude-handoff
candidates.description: Hand the current conversation off to a fresh background agent that picks up the work immediately.

candidates.name: loop-me
candidates.description: Grill me about specs for the workflows I want to build, within this workspace.

candidates.name: setup-ts-deep-modules
candidates.description: Wire dependency-cruiser into a TypeScript repo so each package is a deep module, with implementation hidden in subfolders and reachable only through its entry-point files. User-invoked.

candidates.name: writing-beats
candidates.description: Writing, exploit; assemble raw material into a journey of beats, grounding each term before a beat leans on it.

candidates.name: writing-fragments
candidates.description: Writing, explore: mine raw fragments, no structure yet.

candidates.name: writing-shape
candidates.description: Writing, exploit: shape raw material into an article, paragraph by paragraph.

candidates.name: git-guardrails-claude-code
candidates.description: Set up Claude Code hooks to block dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, branch -D, etc.) before they execute. Use when user wants to prevent destructive git operations, add git safety hooks, or block git push/reset in Claude Code.

candidates.name: migrate-to-shoehorn
candidates.description: Migrate test files from `as` type assertions to @total-typescript/shoehorn. Use when user mentions shoehorn, wants to replace `as` in tests, or needs partial test data.

candidates.name: scaffold-exercises
candidates.description: Create exercise directory structures with sections, problems, solutions, and explainers that pass linting. Use when user wants to scaffold exercises, create exercise stubs, or set up a new course section.

candidates.name: setup-pre-commit
candidates.description: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged (Prettier), type checking, and tests in the current repo. Use when user wants to add pre-commit hooks, set up Husky, configure lint-staged, or add commit-time formatting/typechecking/testing.

candidates.name: grill-me
candidates.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.

candidates.name: grilling
candidates.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

candidates.name: handoff
candidates.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.

candidates.name: teach
candidates.description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.

candidates.name: to-questionnaire
candidates.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

candidates.name: wait-what
candidates.description: Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it.

candidates.name: writing-for-agents
candidates.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

candidates.name: karpathy-guidelines
candidates.description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.

candidates.name: diagnosing-superpowers
candidates.description: Use when a superpowers session went wrong and your human partner wants to know why — repeated work, ignored plans, stumbles, poor results, a skill that didn't fire, "it took too long", "why is it so expensive", "what is it doing" — or wants to build a bug report for the superpowers maintainers, for the current session or a past one identified by id or path, on any harness.

candidates.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
candidates.description: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies

candidates.name: executing-plans
candidates.description: Use when executing an implementation plan in the current session as the implementer yourself — your human partner chose inline execution, or no subagent tool is available

candidates.name: finishing-a-development-branch
candidates.description: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work

candidates.name: receiving-code-review
candidates.description: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation

candidates.name: requesting-code-review
candidates.description: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements

candidates.name: subagent-driven-development
candidates.description: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session

candidates.name: systematic-debugging
candidates.description: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes

candidates.name: test-driven-development
candidates.description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code

candidates.name: using-git-worktrees
candidates.description: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback

candidates.name: using-superpowers
candidates.description: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions

candidates.name: verification-before-completion
candidates.description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always

candidates.name: writing-plans
candidates.description: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code

candidates.name: writing-skills
candidates.description: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment

candidates.name: graphify
candidates.description: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first.
